newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew stays in orbit, navigation to be restored.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew stays in orbit, navigation to be restored.

text.p: The crew of the damaged Mir space station will not abandon it and its latest problem will be fully resolved no later than Saturday, mission director Vladimir Solovyov told reporters on Thursday.

He said Mir's orientation towards the sun would be restored on Friday morning and the gyrodines system which keeps the station in the best position to accumulate energy would be restored the next day. "We are not planning to return the crew, we are planning to continue the flight," he said.

"I expect the ship will be re-oriented by tomorrow morning, by about nine a.m. (0500 GMT)," Solovyov said, adding it would take another day to put gyrodines into full action. "The crew are now being sent to sleep, they are tired."

But Solovyov said the latest crisis probably meant that the repair works in the Spektr module holed in a collision in June 25, would have to be put off once more. He said the date for the work would be decided later.

One of the three-man Russian-U.S. crew mistakenly pulled out a vital computer cable overnight, disrupting the power supply system and plunging the ship into its worst crisis since the near-fatal collision on June 25.

But they gradually succeeded in accumulating sufficient solar power in Mir's batteries to re-start the gyroscopic guidance system. The accumulated energy appeared to make it possible for the crew to restore a vital computer link with Mission Control.
